title: Central versus neutral-late cumulative revenue loss, excluding Australia

claims.text: Extending the climate path with a neutral late-period behavior instead of the fitted autoregressive extension changes the estimated mean cumulative revenue loss for the modeled economies excluding Australia by the separately reported amount. This is a scenario difference reflecting the extension assumption beyond the official forecast horizon, not a causal attribution, and the two alternatives are not assigned occurrence probabilities.

Both scenarios are sensitivity variants of the same dated assessment; the neutral late-period extension variant changes only how the event is extended late in the horizon, holding the rest of the pipeline as in the central case.

limitations: Scenario names are labels, not ratios to the fitted central parameters; the fitted prior scales of central and variant metadata govern any parameter comparison.
Sensitivity alternatives such as the neutral-late extension do not define a calibrated credible interval and are not assigned occurrence probabilities.
The comparison is a scenario difference under different extension assumptions, not causal attribution of revenue outcomes.
The assessment is marked inspection-only with incomplete historical input provenance; frozen inputs were read as stored and no recomputation was performed.
Estimates are signed means (neutral revenue minus event revenue, gains retained); tail measures such as VaR or ES would use positive-part shortfall and are not reported here.
The model covers agriculture, forestry and fishing value added with conditional government revenue transmission; results are not total-economy losses and not sovereign default probabilities.
The extension beyond the official forecast horizon is a modeled assumption and is not an official ENSO forecast.
Price and exchange-rate responses are not modeled; values are in constant 2025 USD with a fixed 2025 exchange rate.
